compressedRanges.label: tax code fields (1-4)
compressedRanges.sourceQuote: The user will now see the tax code fields (1-4) as a list in the Invoice Details and Itemization Summary sections of the invoice.
compressedRanges.notes: SOURCE CHARACTERS: lowercase 'tax code fields', a parenthesised '1-4' with a plain ASCII hyphen and no spaces, preceded in the sentence by the article 'the'. THE MEMBERS ARE EXPANDED MECHANICALLY IN THE LABEL'S OWN VOCABULARY, because the cited file never spells any member out: none of 'VAT Tax Code 1' to 'VAT Tax Code 4' appears anywhere in configure-predefined-tax-codes-6b42509f.md. The member names the raw record had borrowed from concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/available-vat-fields-8b395ce2.md were removed because that borrowing is undecidable: 8b395ce2 documents BOTH a header family ('VAT Tax Code 1' to 4) and a parallel line-item family ('Line Item VAT Tax Code 1' to 4), while the quoted sentence scopes these fields to BOTH the Invoice Details AND the Itemization Summary sections - so the source does not determine which family the members belong to, and importing either set would be a reconciliation the build forbids. An automation must resolve the on-screen names from the rendered page rather than typing these expansions. CONTRADICTED by step-7-optional-configure-predefined-tax-codes-be8bc5b8.md, which names only VAT Tax Code 1 - see the matching contradiction record. Describes downstream invoice fields, not a control on the Tax Administration page, hence appliesTo is empty.

compressedRanges.label: Future Use 1-10
compressedRanges.notes: Ten reserved trailing columns of the Purchase Order Bill-to Address (record type 210) import record, Required? = N. SOURCE CHARACTERS: the label is written with a plain ASCII HYPHEN-MINUS in '1-10' (U+002D), not an en dash, and with title-case 'Future Use'; the Definition cell for this row is not empty but holds a NO-BREAK SPACE (U+00A0), which is why the row renders as ' | \u00a0 | '. THE EXPANSION IS MECHANICAL, NOT QUOTED: the source never enumerates the ten columns, so 'Future Use 1' ... 'Future Use 10' is derived from the compressed form. The underlying column name is rendered 'future\\_use' (escaped underscore) in the Description cell, so the real feed-file column names are more likely future_use1..future_use10 than the title-case display form; the corpus does not state them. These are positional placeholders - an import file must still carry the ten empty columns. This belongs to the PO import record layout, not to the Company Locations page or its import template, so appliesTo is left empty. compressedRanges.label: Level 1 Code - Level 10 Code
compressedRanges.notes: SEPARATOR IS A PLAIN ASCII HYPHEN-MINUS (U+002D) surrounded by single spaces, not an en-dash - verified by grep -F against the source bytes. Each member is the List Management list item short code for one segment level of the hierarchy path ('These are the List Item Short Codes.'), and together they spell the path that selects the default Invoice owner on the Vendor Employee Access import. The expansion is not mechanical guesswork: the identical ten members are written out one row each in concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b51ca3d.md ('Level 1 of the source list attached to the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy.' through Level 10) and in concur-invoice-professional-edition-admin-guides/import-settings-record-type-200-format-c244e3ab.md ('The list item Short Code representing the 1st segment level of the overall hierarchy path.' through the 10th), and the member names here are copied from those enumerations. appliesTo is empty on purpose: these are columns of the Vendor Employee Access import template, not controls on the List Management page, and no Vendor Employee Access Import page exists in the graph to own them. The Group 5B crosscut extract recorded this same range with sourceFile 8b51ca3d, but that file does NOT contain the compressed form - it enumerates all ten - so the citation was moved to 8b4aa547, the only file in which the compressed label actually appears. MERGE PROVENANCE: raised twice in the raw data with two different sourceFiles (8b4aa547 and 8b51ca3d). Collapsed to ONE node after checking both files: only 8b4aa547 contains the compressed string (grep -F -c returns 1 there and 0 in 8b51ca3d, which enumerates all ten rows instead). The two files are still separate real documents - different templates - but only one of them compresses the range, so only one compressed-range node is warranted.

SEPARATOR IS A PLAIN ASCII HYPHEN-MINUS (U+002D) with single spaces, not an en-dash - verified by grep -F.
